questions.q: Which source component would you use to extract from a delimited text file?
options: Flat File Source
OLE DB Source
Raw File Source
Recordset Destination
questions.explain: The Flat File Source reads a single delimited, fixed-width, or ragged-right text file, using a Flat File connection manager.

questions.q: What makes the Raw File source and destination different from every other component pair?
options: They read/write SSIS's own native format, so there's no parsing or translation at all
They only work with SQL Server, never other databases
They require an internet connection to configure
They can only be used inside a For Loop container
questions.explain: Raw File data is already in SSIS's internal representation, making it the fastest possible I/O — but only useful for data a Raw File destination wrote earlier.

questions.q: Which destination has no matching source component, because its whole purpose is to keep data inside the package?
options: Recordset Destination
OLE DB Destination
Flat File Destination
Raw File Destination
questions.explain: Recordset Destination writes rows into an in-memory ADO recordset stored in a package variable, for use by a Script Task or elsewhere in the package — never externally.

questions.q: What is distinctive about the SQL Server Destination compared to the OLE DB Destination?
options: It offers the same high-speed bulk-insert path as the Bulk Insert task, while still allowing transformations first
It can only load data into Excel workbooks
It is the only destination that supports error outputs
It replaces the need for a connection manager entirely
questions.explain: SQL Server Destination is a load-only, bulk-insert specialist for SQL Server tables, faster than OLE DB Destination for that specific case.

questions.q: For Excel 2007 and later workbooks, which source should you use?
options: An OLE DB source with an Excel connection manager
The Excel Source component, exactly as with older Excel versions
The XML Source, since modern Excel files are XML-based
The ADO NET Source only
questions.explain: Excel 2007+ workbooks require a different connection manager than older versions, so you use an OLE DB source rather than the classic Excel source.
